step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend articles if queried by notary or registry

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria — AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es). Customs sub-directorate (Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales) supervises DUA/SAD export clearance and customs registrations for pharmaceutical API outbound consignments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: ES_SL TIN (NIF) procedure: (1) Obtain Certificado de Denominación Social from Registro Mercantil Central to reserve the corporate name. (2) Execute notarial public deed (Escritura de Constitución) before a Spanish Notary, registering NIE for non-EU directors/shareholders where applicable; SL statutory minimum capital is EUR 3,000 under Ley 1/2010, though the simplified 'Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva' variant under Ley 18/2022 may start below that threshold with statutory reserves. (3) File Form 036 (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores) with the competent AEAT Territorial Delegation within 15 calendar days of the deed date to obtain the provisional NIF (format: letter B/C/N + 8 digits + control character). (4) Register the deed with the Provincial Mercantile Registry, then apply via Sede Electrónica for the definitive NIF, which is identical to the provisional NIF. (5) VAT ID (NIF-IVA) is 'ES' + definitive NIF; the same Form 036 triggers registration for Impuesto sobre Sociedades (CIT), IVA, withholding obligations and the AEMPS-linked pharmaceutical wholesale operator status relevant to ISIC 4649. (6) A non-resident parent without a Spanish permanent establishment obtains a non-resident NIF (NIF-NR) through AEAT; where required, Article 91 LIVA and RD 1065/2007 mandate appointment of a tax representative in Spain.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no check-the-box election; ES_SL as a resident SL is compulsorily entity-level taxed on worldwide income (Article 8, Law 27/2014 LIS; general rate 25%, reduced 15% for newly created companies on first EUR 300,000). Elective mechanisms comprise: (i) tax consolidation group election for direct/indirect 70%+ EU/Spain-resident parents (Articles 58-64 LIS); (ii) VAT group (REGE) election under Article 19 Law 37/1992; (iii) patent-box/R&D election under Article 23 LIS (60% gross-revenue exclusion); (iv) reduced-rate election for new-entity entities (Article 29.1 LIS); (v) ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules (Articles 64-68 LIS) impose mandatory deductions/non-inclusion corrections on hybrid instruments, hybrid entities and dual-resident mismatches rather than elective classification; branch (PE) taxation of foreign parents remains entity-level on Spanish-source attributable income, and no pass-through alternative exists for SL shareholders.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (IVA) — Law 37/1992, Royal Decree 1624/1992; harmonized with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; special territorial rules apply to Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 — Spain imposes no general turnover threshold for VAT registration; any person performing taxable business activities in Spanish jurisdiction, including foreign and non-EU suppliers, must register with AEAT before the first taxable supply (Articles 4, 164 LIVA; RD 1624/1992). For EU distance sellers electing the One-Stop-Shop (OSS), the Union-wide threshold is EUR 10,000 of remote cross-border sales; non-EU suppliers are registrable from the first transaction with no threshold. Registration for pharmaceutical API wholesale additionally requires AEMPS import/wholesale authorization (separate administrative license) before taxable activity commences.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain imposes a dual electronic clearance regime: (a) SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) — mandatory real-time transmission for taxpayers with turnover > EUR 6,000,000, VAT groups (REGE) and consolidated groups: all invoice and book-entry records must be transmitted to AEAT via web service/API within 4 calendar days of issue/receipt (extendable to 8 days), replacing paper filing; (b) Verifactu (RD 1007/2023) — all invoicing software used by businesses must preserve invoice authenticity, integrity and legibility via standardized XML records stamped with a QR-type bidirectional 2D code; software suppliers must comply from 1 July 2025. (c) Ley Crea y Crece (Law 18/2022) — phased mandatory B2B e-invoicing for all companies (large > EUR 8,000,000 within one year of the implementing technical order; others within two years). SII non-compliance: Article 198-203 LGT penalties, typically EUR 200 per missing/data block with EUR 1,000 minimum and annual caps; Verifactu software failures attract Article 201 LGT penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT (exemption with right to deduct input VAT) applies under Article 21 LIVA to the definitive export of pharmaceutical API goods from EU customs territory where the exporter is the seller in the customs relationship and the goods physically leave the EU. The departure must be evidenced by a validated customs DUA/SAD declaration; where goods are transferred to a bonded warehouse or storage facility before exit, the exporter may claim a 6-month deadline instead of the standard 3-month dispatch window. Proof of export must be transmitted to AEAT within 60 days after departure evidence is obtained and inscribed in the export ledger. Offshore services related to exported APIs and services digitally delivered to third-country recipients are zero-rated under Articles 69-70 LIVA provided the recipient is established outside the EU and VAT conditions are satisfied; failure to meet these substantive conditions converts the supply to taxable at 21% retroactively.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA / Single Administrative Document) validated by Spanish Customs Surveillance
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing exporter consignment and third-country destination
Inward Remittance Certificate — bank MT103/MT202 or credit advice showing foreign-currency payment credited to the exporter's account
Commercial invoice and ISIC/NAICS-consistent packing list for pharmaceutical APIs
EUR.1 / EUR-MED movement certificate or long-term supplier declaration where preferential origin claimed
Customs transit document (NCTS) where exit occurs through another member state; warehouse receipts if warehousing extension invoked
AEMPS export authorization or inspection certificate where medicinal-product export controls apply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT audit limitation: 4-year administrative prescription (Articles 66-67 LGT). Where export proof is absent or insufficient within the 3-month/6-month statutory window, zero-rating is revoked retroactively to the invoice date: output VAT becomes due with late-payment interest plus Article 191 LGT penalties of 50%-150% of the omitted amount (100%-150% the rise to 2x where fraudulent means are used); wrongly deducted input VAT on clawed-back export supplies is reintegrated with surcharge. Fraudulent documentation (false B/L, bogus DUA, simulated consignee, recycling of exported goods back into Spain) triggers criminal tax fraud under Article 305 Criminal Code where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 per year, punishable by 2-6 years' imprisonment, a fine of 2-6 times the defrauded tax, loss of refunds and subsidies, and legal-person criminal liability under Article 310 bis; aggravated Article 305 bis cases (international organization, misuse of shell entities) carry 4-9 years' imprisonment. Commencement of criminal proceedings suspends the administrative limitation period in favor of AEAT. Non-repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days without economic justification raises transfer-pricing and SII audit-risk flags under Article 16 LIS and may cause AEAT to challenge the economic substance of the export transaction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates under a fully liberalized capital account convertibility regime in which the Euro is convertible without restriction for both current and capital account transactions. Capital account operations are subject exclusively to post-transaction reporting obligations through the Bank of España's SITI system. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted without prior authorization provided they satisfy Spanish withholding tax obligations and beneficial ownership verification under CRS and DAC frameworks. Primary hurdles include rigorous AML/KYC source-of-funds verification, thin capitalization compliance for related-party debt exceeding three-to-one ratios, and timely tax residency certification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spanish exporters must repatriate foreign currency export proceeds denominated in non-Euro currencies to a resident bank account within six months of shipment date. Repatriation is mandatory to satisfy Bank of España foreign exchange reporting requirements. No statutory surrender ratio applies; conversion occurs at prevailing market rates upon deposit. Non-compliance may result in administrative fines up to 300,000 euros and potential criminal sanctions for willful evasion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Spanish law strictly prohibits unlicensed cross-border electronic money issuance by non-resident entities serving Spanish clients. Local EMI licensing under the Electronic Money Institution regime requires Spanish incorporation or branch, minimum capital of 350,000 euros, and continuous Banco de España supervision, rendering offshore digital solutions non-viable without full regulatory compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding via video KYC and qualified electronic signature platforms is permitted for Spanish SL entities under Bank of España guidelines. Physical appearance of directors is required for accounts exceeding transaction thresholds or in heightened AML-risk scenarios such as cross-border API trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk classification arising from pharmaceutical API wholesale involving potential sanctions exposure or complex beneficial ownership structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official wholesale trading license issued by Spanish Ministry of Health, API supplier due diligence reports, import/export customs declarations, beneficial ownership structure documentation, and source-of-wealth affidavits for shareholders

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from shareholders are routed via SWIFT international wire transfers using purpose codes 'CAP' for capital contributions or 'EQTY' for equity injections. Verification protocols require shareholder meeting minutes approving the injection, proof of legitimate funds origin, and post-facto reporting to Banco de España where thresholds are exceeded. All transactions must include tax residency certificates and beneficial ownership declarations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for API purchases utilize SWIFT MT103 messages for direct bank transfers or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit confirmed by correspondent banks. Purpose codes include 'TRADE' for general settlements. LCs must reference exact goods description as 'Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients' per UCP 600 terms. All payments require pre-shipment verification and post-shipment reconciliation with shipping documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts for hedging currency exposure on import purchases
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for USD or CNY exposures
Currency swaps to convert floating rate exposures to fixed rates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts filing and deposit (Cuentas Anuales and, where required, Management Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Registro Mercantil of the company's registered office (Mercantile Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 31 July of the following year. Accounts must be approved by the shareholders meeting within six months after year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registral closure prevents any subsequent corporate filings until accounts are deposited; monetary penalties under Art. 283 Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 up to EUR 60,000; failure to file for two consecutive years may expose the company to administrative dissolution or formal registry removal actions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the six-month period following the tax year-end; for a calendar year-end, from 1 July through 25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 5% plus 1% per additional month up to 20% on tax due; default interest; administrative penalties from 10% to 150% of the omitted tax base; persistent non-filing can lead to forced collection and asset seizure, but does not directly produce corporate strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner (UBO) Declaration confirmation and update (Declaración de Titularidad Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil / Registro de Titularidades Reales administered by the Spanish Registrars (Ministry of Justice regulatory framework)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at least once per fiscal year, concurrent with annual accounts deposit; for a calendar year-end, on or before 31 July. Any share transfer affecting beneficial ownership must be notified promptly, normally within ten working days after the notarized transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or incomplete UBO data blocks registration of corporate acts; infringement sanctions under Ley 10/2010 from EUR 3,005 to EUR 300,000 for willful or serious omissions; false UBO declarations may constitute a criminal offense in aggravated cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 28 February following the calendar/tax year for all suppliers and customers with aggregate annual transactions exceeding EUR 3,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties from EUR 300 to EUR 20,000 for failure to file, late filing, incorrect or incomplete information; in certain cases penalties are based on 2% of the unreported transaction volume. This is an informational return and does not affect corporate status directly.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Pharmacovigilance and Wholesale Distribution Notification for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (AEMPS authorization confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios (AEMPS) / regional health authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, as required by the individual wholesale authorization conditions; generally before the anniversary of the authorization or within the first quarter of each fiscal year; AEMPS guidance controls the applicable submission window.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension or revocation of the wholesale distribution authorization; cessation of permitted API trading; administrative fines under Ley 29/2006 and Royal Decree 824/2010; serious breaches may additionally preclude renewal of the mandatory pharmaceutical license.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit is triggered when a Sociedad de Limitada exceeds at least two of three thresholds on the balance sheet date for two consecutive years: total assets EUR 3,993,000; annual net turnover EUR 7,995,000; average employees 50. Mandatory audit also applies to public-interest entities, groups filing consolidated accounts, and companies so required by shareholders' resolutions or applicable EU-derived legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts must follow Spanish GAAP (Plan General Contable, Real Decreto 1514/2007, as updated); consolidated accounts follow EU-adopted IFRS where applicable. All accounts must comply with Código de Comercio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital, Plan General Contable and applicable disclosure rules; pharmaceutical wholesale activity does not create a separate sector-specific accounting framework unless the entity is listed or has public-interest status.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must maintain a continuous and accurate register of members identifying all direct and indirect natural-person beneficial owners. Under Spanish AML law (Ley 10/2010), the company must file an annual beneficial ownership confirmation through the Registro Mercantil / Registro de Titularidades Reales, normally coinciding with the deposit of annual accounts. Every share transfer in the SL must be documented by notarial deed, recorded in the register of members, and notified to the UBO registry within ten working days. Annual confirmation must reconcile the final register against the declared UBO chain; discrepancies delay or block corporate filings.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350–1,200 per year including registered office lease or agent services and customary compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–10,500 per year for a mid-sized pharmaceutical wholesale distribution entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% for newly established entities in the first two years with taxable base; tax credits for R&D, innovation, and job creation; participation exemption for qualifying dividends.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically via the Spanish Tax Agency's online portal (Sede Electrónica de la AEAT).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days following the 6-month period after the fiscal year-end (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, deadline is July 25 of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the tax base after adjustments to accounting profit, including transfer pricing adjustments and tax-exempt income.
Apply the standard 25% rate, or 15% if the entity qualifies as newly established and meets the conditions.
Calculate tax before deductions, credits, and withholdings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholdings and payments on account (Retenciones y pagos a cuenta)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any withholdings on income and quarterly installment payments (Modelo 202) made during the year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund (Cuota diferencial)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resulting amount after deducting withholdings and payments; if positive, pay by the deadline; if negative, claim refund.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: 5% of tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, 20% after 12 months, plus late payment interest. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% (general non-resident rate; 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if conditions met).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the home tax authority and submit it to the Spanish payer or the AEAT. The payer must retain the TRC and apply the reduced rate at source. If the reduced rate is not applied, the non-resident may file a refund claim using Modelo 210 within the statutory period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 24% for royalties and interest (19% for EU/EEA residents). Treaty rates may reduce to 0-10% depending on the jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if net turnover ≥ €10 million; Master File required if group consolidated turnover ≥ €45 million; Country-by-Country Report if group consolidated turnover ≥ €750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain applies general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles. A company is tax resident if incorporated in Spain, has its registered office in Spain, or has its place of effective management in Spain. No specific ESR, but lack of economic substance may trigger recharacterization and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of taxable income or overstatement of deductions, including false transfer pricing documentation or omission of taxable transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% to 150% of the tax evaded, plus late payment interest. Criminal prosecution for tax evasion exceeding €120,000 may lead to imprisonment up to 6 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for tax debts if involved in evasion. Travel bans and civil asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a shell company with no real business activity, employees, or premises, used to channel profits or avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions, denial of treaty benefits, and penalties up to 150% of the tax underpaid. The company may be deemed tax resident in Spain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for civil restitution and may face criminal charges for fraudulent insolvency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling funds from illegal activities, failing to implement AML controls, or conducting transactions with sanctioned entities in the pharmaceutical API trade.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €10 million or 10% of the funds involved, and criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 6 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face imprisonment, criminal fines, and bans from holding directorships.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain transfer pricing documentation or applying non-arm's length prices in cross-border transactions, leading to profit shifting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties of 15% on the adjusted amount (or 20% if documentation is not provided), plus late payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for penalties if they were involved in pricing decisions.
